claims: The company serves six fleet sectors: waste collection, highways, construction, cash in transit, transport and logistics, and blue light.
The company's publicly named UK clients include Biffa, FCC Environment, Canenco (Canterbury City Council), Cardtronics and Stratford-on-Avon District Council.
In September 2025 the company and Biffa trialled Binsight, a connected food-waste bin sensor system, for Stratford-on-Avon District Council.
Canenco, which runs Canterbury City Council's environmental services, deployed the company's Defend Connected Live 4G DVR vehicle cameras across its fleet in 2022.
The World Health Organization awarded the company a service contract valued at $136,100 on 9 December 2020.
Oxfam uses the company's tracpoint software for vehicle tracking, movement planning and fuel monitoring across its regional operations.
The company reports that its platform links vehicle tracking data into back-office systems including CRM, payroll and maintenance scheduling.
The company offers rolling monthly contracts that let clients add and remove vehicles as their needs change.
FFAVS Ltd's Companies House accounts report an average of 22 employees for the year to 31 May 2025, unchanged from the previous year.
The company names UK clients including UK Power Networks, Camfaud, Breedon, Opex Logistics, Pallet Plus, Kaefer and Conway Bailey Transport.
OPEX Logistics expanded its Fleet Focus camera system rollout to 77 vehicles.
In July 2026 Bretts Transport equipped 24 vehicles with the company's cloud-connected four-way camera systems.
The company reports customers in 17 countries.
In November 2025 the company integrated its platform with Shippeo for a transport visibility project covering more than 500 trailers operating between the UK and Northern Ireland.
In November 2025 the company integrated its platform with Shippeo's supply chain visibility platform for a project covering more than 500 trailers operating between the UK and Northern Ireland.
In October 2025 the company launched the Teltonika FTC880 IP69K-rated GPS tracker on its platform.
In August 2025 the company announced a partnership to supply connected dash cameras and telematics to Thames Valley Transport.
The company's vehicle technicians are TASSA-certified and Thatcham-approved installers of vehicle trackers and immobilisation systems.
The company reports that its platform supports tracking hardware from Teltonika, Queclink, Concox and Digital Matter, among more than 3,000 compatible devices.
